doc: Built-in FTS5 tokenizers: unicode61 (default), ascii (byte-level), porter (stemming wrapper). Owns the Fts5Tokenizer / Fts5TokenStream surface consumed by the index and query parts. Determinism across targets is a hard correctness gate.

Fts5Tokenizer.doc: An immutable tokenizer instance. Built from a name + arg list. Cheap to clone; safe to call from any context.

Fts5TokenStream.doc: Pull iterator yielding Fts5Token records in document order. Borrows its source text — caller MUST keep the text alive for the stream's lifetime.

Fts5Token.doc: One token. `bytes` is the folded form persisted to the index; (start, end) are byte offsets into the original input.

Fts5TokenMode.doc: Tokenization mode. v1: Document and Query produce identical streams for every built-in tokenizer; the distinction is reserved for future synonym support.

Unicode61Args.doc: Parsed unicode61 argument set. `categories_add` and `categories_drop` accumulate +CC / -CC modifiers. `tokenchars` and `separators` carry the literal-character overrides.

PorterArgs.doc: Recursive porter (porter wrapping porter) is rejected at create time, so `base_kind` is constrained to Unicode61 or Ascii.

Fts5Tokenizer.name: create
Fts5Tokenizer.doc: Build a tokenizer from a `tokenize=` value string already split into [name, arg0, arg1, …].

Fts5Tokenizer.name: tokenize
Fts5Tokenizer.doc: Open a token stream over `text`. The stream borrows `text`; caller must keep it alive.

Fts5Tokenizer.name: name
Fts5Tokenizer.doc: Stable lowercase name of the tokenizer family (unicode61 / ascii / porter). Used by the index part to persist into t_config.

Fts5Tokenizer.name: args
Fts5Tokenizer.doc: Round-trip the original argument list. Used to persist the exact tokenize= value into t_config so a query-time re-create produces an identical tokenizer.

Fts5TokenStream.name: next
Fts5TokenStream.doc: Advance and return the next token; absent when exhausted.

porter_stem_ascii.doc: Apply Porter (1980) Steps 1a/1b/1c/2/3/4/5a/5b to a pure-ASCII lowercase word. Words shorter than 3 chars or containing any byte ≥ 0x80 must NOT call this — caller filters first. Pure function; same input → same output on every target.

unicode61_fold.doc: Apply Unicode-6.1 case-folding (and optional NFKD-strip when remove_diacritics≥1) to one input code point. Output is a sequence of one or more code points (full case folding can expand).

unicode61_is_token_char.doc: Return true iff the code point is a token character under unicode61's default classification (L*, N*, Co), as modified by `categories_add` / `categories_drop` / `tokenchars` / `separators`.
